brief:
Gazans continue to endure severe shortages and loss of privacy more than a year after a ceasefire agreement, according to an account in The Guardian. Residents, including the writer Akram al-Sourani, queue daily for water and describe feeling estranged from their former lives and from themselves. The conditions suggest a return to normalcy remains elusive despite the halt in active hostilities.

Al-Sourani describes a landscape where basic services remain unavailable and community bonds have fractured under prolonged strain. Residents express a sense of disconnection from the lives they once knew, marking a departure from established patterns of daily existence.

title: Gaza residents face persistent deprivation a year after ceasefire
